description: Four-shaft plain-weave double width with the fold on the left (one shuttle, top, bottom, bottom, top, as Ply's double-weave generator writes it), 480 ends by 8 picks, sett 24 ends per inch in the reed (both layers together) from the file's [WARP] Spacing=0.0416667. In the reed it is 20 in wide, folded; opened out it is about 40 in. The loom check uses the folded width the loom holds: it fits a 24 in loom (opened, 40 in would not) and not a 16 in one.

diagnostics.message: This draft threads 4 shafts; Four-shaft jack loom has 4.
This draft uses 4 treadles; Four-shaft jack loom has 6.
No pick presses more than one treadle at a time.
This draft's tie-up is written for a rising shed (the marked shafts go up), as a jack loom works.

Woven double width with the fold on the left, this draft is 20 in wide in the reed, folded (480 ends at 24 ends per inch, from the file); opened out, the cloth is about 40 in. Four-shaft jack loom weaves up to 24 in.
Sley the 12-dent reed 2 per dent for 24 ends per inch.
This draft threads 4 shafts; Table loom has 8.
On Table loom you lift the shafts with hand levers for each pick, so treadles do not limit this draft.
